notes:
Summary: mid-market multi-tenant agent SaaS (in-app support agents + proactive outreach). Evaluating Redwood Hosted API first (fast onboarding) then Dedicated for predictable latency and SLA. High-level constraints: per-tenant quotas + billing, streaming stability for tool-calling flows, EU data residency for subset of customers.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (AE Maya) — product overview, interest in streaming + tool calling.
- 2026-02-01: Demo — streaming chat with function calls; customer liked function-calling hooks but saw jitter in long-running streams.
- 2026-02-18: POC kickoff (hosted) — 2-week baseline to collect latency/p99, token cost metrics. Fireflies: ffly_2026-02-18_8932.
- 2026-02-25: SE deep-dive with Diego — discussed batching, KV cache, and prefix caching to reduce token usage. Identified need for per-tenant cache isolation.
- 2026-03-02: Observability review — they want token-level cost breakdown by tenant and route; flagged console gaps. Fireflies: ffly_2026-03-02_9104.

Technical requirements / acceptance criteria:
- Workload: multi-tenant chat agents, heavy tool-calling (CRM lookup, ticket patching).
- Latency SLO: first-token streaming start <= 200ms p95 under normal load; tail latency p99 target < 600ms.
- Throughput: steady 40-60 RPS across fleet, burst capacity to 200 RPS during spikes.
- Streaming stability: no >1% dropped streams or reconnections during 72-hour soak.
- Rate limits: per-tenant QPS + token quotas, ability to set burst windows and soft-fail (degraded streaming to short responses).
- Routing/fallback: prefer local EU region for EU customers, automatic fallback to cheaper model under overload but must preserve tool-calling semantics.
- Security: Okta SAML SSO, audit logs exported to customer SIEM, KMS integration for key management, data residency flag for EU customer records.

POC notes / findings so far:
- Hosted API: fastest to demo; telemetry shows average first-byte ~160ms but spikes to 700ms during peaks. Streaming reconnections observed (approx 0.8%).
- Batching & caching: suggestion from SE reduced token cost by ~18% in synthetic runs. Need per-tenant cache partitions to avoid leakage.
- Dedicated interest: customer wants committed capacity if Dedicated can bring p99 below 500ms consistently and reduce jitter. Pricing sensitivity: wants traceability of committed units -> price per RPS and overage rules.
- Console gaps: per-tenant quota config and per-tenant billing slices not visible; requires either API-driven controls or console UI.

Quotes / paraphrases from stakeholders:
- "We need predictable latency for our paying customers — bursting is fine but the tail kills the UX." — Head of Product
- "If Dedicated can guarantee the SLOs and per-tenant billing slices, this becomes an easy procurement case." — CTO

Next steps agreed:
- Run 72-hour stress POC on Hosted (Mar 7-10) capturing p50/p95/p99, streaming reconnection rate, and per-route token cost.
- SE to provide dedicated sizing recommendation for committed GPUs and an initial pricing band by Mar 12.
- Security: share SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration guide; customer to run internal legal review (target complete by Mar 25).
- Follow-up call to review POC metrics and Dedicated pricing (owner: Maya) — schedule week of Mar 16.

Other notes / misc:
- Linked docs: drive://redwood/poc/pegasus-hosted-vs-dedicated-deck.pdf (pricing + sizing), drive://redwood/security/pegasus-security-questions.xlsx (security Q/A).
- Open support tickets: ENG-1347 (streaming reconnect root cause), SEC-4021 (SOC2 evidence packaging).
- Decision drivers: latency/p99 stability > per-token unit cost. If Dedicated reduces jitter and Redwood provides per-tenant quotas + console billing, likely move to annual committed Dedicated contract.

Short-term blockers: Okta timing, console quota UI, finance sign-off. Long-term: data residency controls for EU customers and full SOC2 artefact exchange.
